provenance.title: Rheumatic heart disease — secondary prophylaxis, echo referral and ARF recognition
provenance.primarySource: WHO Technical Report Series — Rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease; WHF criteria for acute rheumatic fever; Zimbabwe RHD programme guidance (published summaries)
provenance.why: Rheumatic heart disease remains prevalent in Zimbabwe. Recurrent streptococcal pharyngitis without benzathine penicillin prophylaxis progresses valve damage silently. Echo quantifies severity and guides referral for valve intervention — this pack prompts prophylaxis adherence and echo referral, not surgical scheduling.

sourceVerification.note: WHO RHD guidance is NOT vendored under docs/reference/who-dak/MANIFEST.json. Authored against published WHO/WHF RHD and secondary-prophylaxis recommendations; ships ENGINEERING_SEED until primary text is vendored and MOHCC ratifies prophylaxis interval and echo referral thresholds.

rules.name: Secondary prophylaxis due — benzathine penicillin G
rules.message: Secondary prophylaxis overdue — give benzathine penicillin G now.
rules.explanation: Secondary prophylaxis with benzathine penicillin G every 3–4 weeks prevents recurrent acute rheumatic fever and slows valve destruction. Missing a dose opens a window for streptococcal infection and further scarring — the commonest preventable cause of RHD progression in adolescents and young adults.
rules.requiredAction: Administer intramuscular benzathine penicillin G at the ratified weight-based dose now, record the date, and register the patient on the RHD prophylaxis schedule with recall.

adaptation.whoStatement: Patients with established RHD should receive regular benzathine penicillin to prevent recurrent ARF.
adaptation.nationalStatement: 28-day overdue threshold is a placeholder pending national recall interval ratification.

testCases.name: RHD and 30 days since last dose — prophylaxis due fires
RHD and 14 days since last dose — not due
days since last dose not supplied — must not fire

rules.name: Penicillin allergy — use the ratified alternative prophylaxis regimen
rules.message: Penicillin allergy with overdue prophylaxis — use the national alternative (e.g. azithromycin).
rules.explanation: True penicillin allergy excludes benzathine penicillin. Erythromycin or azithromycin prophylaxis is less effective but better than none — stopping prophylaxis entirely because of allergy without an alternative is a common failure mode.
rules.requiredAction: Confirm allergy history, start the ratified non-penicillin secondary prophylaxis regimen, and document the reason benzathine penicillin is contraindicated.
sourceRefs: WHO RHD guideline — penicillin allergy alternatives

adaptation.whoStatement: Alternative antibiotics may be used when penicillin is contraindicated.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Prompt fires when prophylaxis is overdue AND allergy documented — avoids silent gap in allergic patients.
adaptation.rationale: Couples overdue prophylaxis with documented penicillin allergy so allergic patients are not left without an alternative regimen prompt.

testCases.name: RHD allergic and overdue — alternative fires
RHD allergic but prophylaxis recent — does not fire
no allergy — benzathine rule owns this

rules.name: Known RHD without recent echo — refer for echocardiography
rules.message: Rheumatic heart disease — echocardiography overdue or never performed.
rules.explanation: Valve severity in RHD changes silently. Echocardiography quantifies regurgitation or stenosis, guides prophylaxis intensity, anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation, and timing of valve intervention referral. Clinical examination alone misses moderate disease.
rules.requiredAction: Refer for transthoracic echocardiography and cardiology review. If symptoms (dyspnoea, palpitations, syncope) are present, expedite referral regardless of interval.

adaptation.whoStatement: Regular echocardiographic surveillance is recommended in RHD.
adaptation.nationalStatement: 12-month echo interval and NEVER sentinel encoded pending national ratification.
adaptation.rationale: Sets a national 12-month / NEVER echo surveillance interval pending MOHCC ratification of the recall schedule.

testCases.name: RHD echo 14 months ago — referral fires
RHD echo 6 months ago — not due

rules.name: Acute rheumatic fever suspected — treat streptococcus and start prophylaxis planning
rules.message: Acute rheumatic fever suspected — treat streptococcal infection and plan secondary prophylaxis.
rules.explanation: Acute rheumatic fever after group A streptococcal pharyngitis is the upstream event that causes RHD. Treating the acute episode with penicillin and enrolling the patient on long-term benzathine prophylaxis prevents the first or recurrent valve injury.
rules.requiredAction: Treat acute streptococcal infection per protocol, manage carditis/arthritis/chorea as indicated, and register for benzathine penicillin secondary prophylaxis before discharge.

adaptation.whoStatement: Acute rheumatic fever requires antibiotic treatment of streptococcal infection and initiation of secondary prophylaxis.

testCases.name: ARF not suspected — does not fire
ARF not assessed — must not fire
